acceptance: A test covers a single-quoted interpreter path with a space on Linux
The preflight still refuses a missing or non-executable interpreter
context: Found by triage of the 2026-10-08 Windows 3.12 log. Split out because the script gates all agent writes.
description: pre-commit writes INSTALL_PYTHON with shell quoting when the interpreter path contains characters such as a backslash or colon (for example INSTALL_PYTHON='D:\a\BenchBox\...\python.exe'). scripts/agent_write_preflight.sh (about lines 177-178) takes the raw text after '=', quotes included, and tests it with [ ! -x ... ], so it reports 'shared pre-commit hook is not usable'. The same refusal would hit any POSIX interpreter path containing a space. Strip one pair of surrounding single quotes after reading the value (hook_interpreter=${hook_interpreter#\\'}; hook_interpreter=${hook_interpreter%\\'}). This script gates every agent write on every platform, so test it with a quoted and an unquoted path and confirm on a Windows run that [ -x "D:\\a\\...\\python.exe" ] passes under Git Bash. tests/unit/test_agent_write_preflight.py test_configured_hook_allows_linked_worktree_commit currently fails on windows-latest 3.12 and later steps of that test may reveal more.
